newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Clark and Peters work on housing initiative.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Clark and Peters work on housing initiative.

text.p: Labour leader Helen Clark and New Zealand First leader Winston Peters on Friday broke their silence over details of coalition negotiations, saying the two parties had discussed housing policy at talks on Thursday.
Clark told Reuters she had advocated a joint approach with New Zealand First over the government's housing policy.
She had raised the issue with New Zealand First during Thursday's meeting after receiving details of a big state house rent rise faced by one of her constituents.
"I did raise it yesterday. State rentals are a huge issue in my electorate. Property prices have gone through the roof and rents with them," Clark said.

"I did raise it at the New Zealand First talks in the afternoon that I felt it was obviously going to take a while to form a government but there was a fairly desperate situation developing. Winston Peters was genuinely concerned at the scale of the increase."

She said the constituent, who had five children and whose wife had a disability, faced a rise from $255 a week to $355 and had been told he could expect only a $25 increase in his accommodation supplement.
Asked if Labour and New Zealand First were going to make a joint approach to the caretaker National government, Clark said: "That is what I have suggested."
"I think he (Peters) was genuinely shocked. What we undertook was to get more information next week."
Asked if the approach was over a single constituent, Clark said: "No, it is the generic thing."
Speaking on a radio talkback show, Peters confirmed the discussion on housing policy.

"I can tell you this here and now, and I am not speaking out of turn. I think it is fair to say that I discussed this with Helen Clark yesterday. We should have a report hopefully Monday or Tuesday next week," Peters said in response to a question about rises in state housing rents.

A spokesman for Clark said Labour would advocate an interim freeze to rises in state house rentals -- a key component of New Zealand First's housing policy. Labour's policy was to relate state house rentals to income.

New Zealand First holds the balance of power after the October 12 general election and is negotiating with Labour and the conservative caretaker National party government over the shape of the new administration.
